rows.paragraph: Every integer unimodular matrix is a finite product of these operations. To prove this, apply the finite Euclidean row-and-column procedure of the handle-chain chapter, \cref{courseIII:integral-handle-chains-and-signed-incidences:section-4}, to a square matrix \(V\) with determinant \(\pm1\). It gives diagonal entries with successive divisibility and product of absolute values \(1\); hence each diagonal entry has absolute value \(1\). The retained operations are row and column additions by integer multiples, permutations and sign changes. Reverse their finite list. Multiplication on either side by an elementary matrix is itself a matrix product, so reversing the list expresses \(V\) as a product of the indicated generators. This argument records each multiplier and never replaces the original \(V\).
